Feature: DRAFT - A4 2026-11-02 - to be revised by A6 auditor and science agents (A1-A3, A5)

User benefit: Hands-free set log; reps, set start/end, rep duration
What is actually measured: EMG burst envelope (rectified/RMS) on one muscle + puck IMU accel/gyro on the limb segment carrying the band
Evidence strength: H; I (EMG/IMU rep segmentation is routine in lab work); moderate that it is achievable, none for TENSR specifically
Hardware fit: Good for EMG bursts on any worn muscle. IMU alone is weak where the band's segment is static in the exercise (biceps/triceps in curls/pushdowns: upper arm static; quad in leg extension: thigh static; chest in bench press: torso static). Fusion needed
Calibration: Per-exercise thresholds or adaptive envelope threshold; no per-user MVC needed
Expected limitations: Partial reps, pauses, rest-pause, isometric holds, cheating reps; co-contraction from stabilising; low-load sets with small bursts; crosstalk from neighbouring muscles producing bursts in other exercises
Validation required: Count agreement vs video-annotated reps across >=10 exercises, >=20 users, both sexes, range of skinfolds; report % exact sets and per-rep F1, by exercise; subject-wise held-out evaluation

Feature: Electrical-activity duration (burst duration per rep, total active time per set)
User benefit: Objective record of how long the muscle was electrically active
What is actually measured: Time EMG envelope exceeds an on/off threshold
Evidence strength: I/M; moderate that onset/offset detection works in lab; threshold choice changes values (textile vs gel electrodes gave systematically longer bursts in Colyer2018)
Hardware fit: Fits; needs sample rate high enough for clean envelope (>=1 kSPS preferable) and stable baseline
Calibration: Baseline (rest) noise per session for threshold
Expected limitations: Depends on threshold, electrode contact, noise floor; tonic activity in stabilising roles means 'active' != 'moving the load'
Validation required: Agreement with reference gel-electrode EMG onsets and with video phases; test-retest across days
Recommendation: Suitable to prototype (as a raw descriptive number, not a quality score)

User benefit: Familiar coaching metric without a stopwatch
What is actually measured: Proxy only: EMG-active time and/or IMU segment-motion time. Tension itself (force) is not measured
Evidence strength: H; mechanical TUT needs force/position; electrical activity duration is a different quantity. Evidence that TUT per se drives growth is for A1 to grade
Hardware fit: Partial: IMU sees movement only if band's segment moves; EMG duration available always
Expected limitations: Electrical TUT != mechanical TUT (holds at lockout with low EMG, eccentric phases with low EMG per force); naming it 'tension' overstates
Validation required: Compare to video/encoder-defined set duration and phase timing; state which definition is shown
Recommendation: Suitable to prototype if labelled as 'set/rep duration' or 'active time'; 'time under tension' wording is misleading in its proposed form

Feature: Relative activation trends (amplitude within a set / session)
User benefit: See whether the muscle is working harder across reps of a set
What is actually measured: RMS/ARV amplitude in uV, single location, unnormalised or normalised to a reference contraction
Evidence strength: I; moderate that amplitude rises across a submaximal set to failure in lab; amplitude-force relationship is nonlinear and muscle-specific; between-session CV of ARV ~41-43% even in lab (Colyer2018)
Hardware fit: Fits for within-set, same-wear trends; not for between-day absolute comparison without normalisation
Calibration: Within-set: none. Between-day: reference contraction (submax isometric or MVC) every wear
Expected limitations: Electrode impedance drift (sweat), band shifting, subcutaneous fat, crosstalk; amplitude falls with lower load (drop sets) independent of fatigue
Validation required: Within-session repeatability, between-day reliability (ICC, SEM, MDC) with and without normalisation
Recommendation: Suitable to prototype (within-set relative trend only)

Feature: Activation % ('is the target muscle doing the work')
What is actually measured: Same amplitude signal; % requires a denominator (MVC or reference) for this muscle at this placement
Evidence strength: I; limited. One channel cannot apportion work between synergists; %MVC is position- and velocity-dependent; MVC in untrained users unreliable
Hardware fit: Poor for the stated claim: no synergist or antagonist channel, no force
Calibration: MVC or reference contraction each wear, per exercise posture
Expected limitations: Crosstalk at 25.4 mm IED with 7 mm studs; joint-angle dependence; normalisation error; cannot say 'target muscle did X% of the work'
Validation required: Compare against multi-channel reference EMG and dynamometer; show per-user between-day MDC
Recommendation: Unsupported or misleading in its proposed form (as 'share of work'). A within-set relative amplitude trend is the defensible subset

What is actually measured: IMU segment angular velocity sign (when the band's segment moves) and/or EMG amplitude pattern
Evidence strength: I; moderate for IMU phase detection on a moving segment; very limited for EMG-only phase detection
Hardware fit: Exercise-dependent: works for delt raises, squats, lunges (segment moves); not for curls/pushdowns/bench/leg extension where the worn segment is static
Calibration: Per exercise; orientation of puck on limb
Expected limitations: Static-segment exercises give no phase signal; EMG-only split ambiguous because eccentric EMG is lower per unit force
Validation required: Phase timing vs video/encoder across exercise list; report which exercises are unsupported
Recommendation: Potentially useful after substantial validation (restricted exercise list)

Feature: Within-set fatigue trend (MDF/MNF decline, amplitude rise)
User benefit: See fatigue accumulate rep by rep
What is actually measured: Spectral indices (MDF/MNF) per rep window + amplitude; dynamic, nonstationary signal
Evidence strength: I/M; moderate that MDF falls across sets to failure in lab with gel electrodes; MDF shifts depend on load and tempo (bench studies: larger MDF drop at lighter loads; load x tempo interaction, Yan2025); MDF unrelated to velocity loss in Zhao2025
Hardware fit: Constrained: at the 500 SPS bring-up rate the ADS1292R sinc3 filter is -3 dB at ~131 Hz and Nyquist is 250 Hz, so the 120 Hz 'fresh' MDF cannot be measured faithfully. Needs >=1-2 kSPS. Electrode orientation vs fibres unrecorded; 25.4 mm IED puts the bipolar spatial-filter dip (v/d) at ~118-157 Hz, inside the MDF band
Calibration: Per-user, per-muscle, per-exercise baseline (first reps); fixed window aligned to rep phase / joint-angle range
Expected limitations: Joint angle, contraction velocity, load, recruitment, electrode shift over innervation zone, temperature, sweat change MDF independently of fatigue; dry electrode noise
Validation required: Rep-level MDF slope reliability; agreement with reference gel EMG at SENIAM placement; dependence on tempo/load tested explicitly
Recommendation: Potentially useful after substantial validation (display as a relative within-set trend, not a fatigue %)

User benefit: Stop sets at intended effort without guessing
What is actually measured: Model output from EMG features (+ IMU) predicting reps remaining; no load input, no bar velocity
Evidence strength: H; very limited/none for sEMG-based RIR prediction (no peer-reviewed sEMG RIR model found in this search; preprints use IMU; velocity-based RIR needs individual equations, Garcia-Ramos2018)
Hardware fit: Constrained: single channel, no load, IMU on limb not bar; MDF requires >=1 kSPS
Calibration: Individual calibration sets to failure per exercise likely required
Expected limitations: Load and tempo change MDF trajectory; failure definition varies; a classifier can learn set length/rep count rather than physiology; RIR self-report error
Validation required: Prospective, subject-wise held-out prediction of reps-to-failure vs observed failure, MAE in reps with LoA, beaten against simple baselines (rep count vs known RM; IMU velocity loss); multiple exercises, loads, tempos

Feature: Set score / 'did this set reach failure'
What is actually measured: Post-hoc classification of end-of-set EMG features
Evidence strength: H; very limited. End-of-set classification is easier than live RIR but still unvalidated; the brief's 20-30-set test is underpowered and confounded by set length
Expected limitations: Failure sets are longer and have more reps, so duration alone may separate groups; 'true failure' labelling unreliable
Validation required: Classifier vs duration/rep-count baseline; multiple users; held-out subjects and days; report sensitivity/specificity with CIs

Feature: Between-set recovery estimate / muscle-driven rest timer
User benefit: Know when to start the next set
What is actually measured: MDF/amplitude recovery during rest (resting EMG is near noise floor; would need a brief test contraction) + elapsed time
Evidence strength: I/M; limited. MDF returns towards baseline within ~1-10 min while amplitude/force capacity can remain altered; MDF recovery != performance readiness
Hardware fit: Plain timer: trivially fits. Recovery-driven: needs a standardised probe contraction each rest
Expected limitations: Resting signal has no spectrum to measure; probe contraction adds fatigue; recovery of performance depends on systemic factors not seen by one channel
Validation required: Show that recommended rest predicts next-set reps better than fixed rest (randomised within-subject trial)
Recommendation: Rest timer (elapsed time, auto-start at set end): Suitable to prototype. 'Recovery-driven' timer: Research-only

What is actually measured: Two bands, one per side: amplitude/MDF per side
Evidence strength: H/I; limited. Bilateral amplitude differences reflect placement, skinfold and impedance as much as output
Hardware fit: Not possible with one band. Two bands need: shared timebase (BLE timestamp sync to ~10 ms for rep alignment), mirrored anatomical placement and orientation, per-side normalisation (reference contraction), matched electrode condition
Expected limitations: EMG asymmetry != strength/size asymmetry; between-day CV of amplitude is large
Validation required: Two-band agreement vs dynamometer asymmetry; repeatability of asymmetry index across re-donning
Recommendation: Research-only (and not deliverable on one-band hardware)

What is actually measured: EMG burst shape, amplitude consistency, IMU segment motion smoothness/ROM
Evidence strength: H; very limited. No validated definition of 'contraction quality' from one channel
Hardware fit: Partial: segment ROM only on moving segments; no joint angle
Expected limitations: Undefined construct; risk of rewarding EMG amplitude, which is not the goal of training
Validation required: First define the construct and its reference (expert video rating, joint kinematics), then test agreement
Recommendation: Unsupported or misleading in its proposed form; narrow IMU-based items (rep ROM consistency on a moving segment) potentially useful after validation

What is actually measured: Composite of acute EMG features; no measure of growth
Evidence strength: H; none linking a wearable EMG composite to longitudinal hypertrophy. Acute EMG amplitude differences are not evidence of long-term growth (SHARED-STANDARDS rule 4)
Hardware fit: No hardware measures muscle size (A-mode ultrasound is a v3 research idea)
Expected limitations: Would claim an outcome the device cannot observe
Validation required: Longitudinal trial with ultrasound/MRI outcome showing the score predicts growth beyond sets-to-near-failure counting
Recommendation: Unsupported or misleading in its proposed form

Feature: Weekly volume per muscle (sets, reps, load-free)
What is actually measured: Counts of detected sets/reps for whichever muscle wore the band; no load, no exercise identity unless user tags
Evidence strength: I; moderate for counting given validated rep detection
Hardware fit: One band per session covers one muscle; a 'whole split' needs the band moved or multiple bands
Expected limitations: Untracked muscles are invisible; 'hard sets' requires a validated effort estimate
Validation required: Agreement with manual log over 4+ weeks
Recommendation: Suitable to prototype (as counts with user tagging); 'stimulus per muscle' Unsupported in proposed form
